[Package]
Name = "jki_lib_state_machine"
Version = "2024.0.1.14"

Display Name = "JKI State Machine"

[Description]
Description = "The JKI State Machine is a template you can use for quickly creating your own LabVIEW applications. This is the very same template that is used by the JKI team, nearly every day, and is the result of years of refinement by our team of LabVIEW experts. We encourage you to post any questions or comments to the JKI Software Forums. There you will find an active community of JKI software users, as well as JKI team members.\0D\0A\0D\0AHow to use:\0D\0A\0D\0AFind the JKI State Machine in the palettes\0D\0A1) Functions >> JKI Toolkits >> JKI State Machine\0D\0A\0D\0AUse QuickDrop to place a JKI State Machine on the block diagram\0D\0A1)  Press Control+Space then type "JKI"\0D\0A2) choose the "JKI State Machine" option that appears\0D\0A\0D\0ALaunch the JKI State Machine Explorer by either\0D\0AA) Right-click on a State String, Case Structure, or Event Structure to launch JKI SM Editor\0D\0AB) Press Control+Space then Control+J when you're on the block diagram of a VI containing a JKI SM\0D\0A\0D\0A\0D\0AUsing the Right-click menu on the JKI SM Parts for increased productivity:\0D\0A- Select an item in the tree to make that frame visible\0D\0A- Click back and forward to navigate the history\0D\0A- Drag and drop frames to reorganize the order\0D\0A- Right-click on items in the tree-view to rename, duplicate, delete, etc.\0D\0A- Right-click on a state string and choose Goto State Frame to jump to that frame of the JKI SM.\0D\0A- Right click on a state string or frame and choose Find Callers to find all callers of a state\0D\0A- Right-click on a bundle or unbundle by name and choose Find Data Accessors to find all accessors of the data.\0D\0A\0D\0ASpecial thanks to Jim Carmody for open sourcing his CaseSelect tool as a launching off point for the JKI SM Editor."
Summary = "JKI State Machine"
License = "BSD"
Copyright = "Copyright (C) 2005-2024, JKI"
Distribution = ""
Vendor = "JKI"
URL = "http://jki.net/state-machine/"
Packager = "JKI"
Demo = "FALSE"
Release Notes = "What's New in JKI State Machine 2024\0D\0A\0D\0AThis is a major new release with a focus on a few significant improvements:\0D\0A\0D\0A1. New State Enqueuing VIs:, to make it easier to conditionally enqueue states based on boolean logic and periodic timing (in a way that produces readable code).\0D\0A2. Improved Error Handling: to include information about the state where the error occurred as well as clear (or handling) "warnings" (non-zero `error code` but `status` is False).\0D\0A3. Upgrading source code to LV2020: to make it easier for community members to contribute and for the development team to take advantage of newer LabVIEW features.\0D\0A\0D\0AThere are also some other nice improvements to the template and misc fixes.\0A\0AUpdates to JKI State Machine Editor.\0A\0AKnown Issues:\0AIn LabVIEW 2024, changes to how right-click menu references are handled have caused the JKI State Machine Helper utilities to be inaccessible via the right-click menu. However, you can still access the JKI State Machine Helper using the Ctrl+J Quick Drop shortcut. JKI is working with NI to restore full support as soon as possible. Other LabVIEW versions remain unaffected."

We encourage you to post any questions or comments to the JKI Software Forums. There you will find an active community of JKI software users, as well as JKI team members.\0A\0AHow to use:\0A\0AFind the JKI State Machine in the palettes\0A1) Functions >> JKI Toolkits >> JKI State Machine\0A\0AUse QuickDrop to place a JKI State Machine on the block diagram\0A1)  Press Control+Space then type "JKI"\0A2) choose the "JKI State Machine" option that appears\0A\0ALaunch the JKI State Machine Explorer by either\0D\0AA) Right-click on a State String, Case Structure, or Event Structure to launch JKI SM Editor\0D\0AB) Press Control+Space then Control+J when you're on the block diagram of a VI containing a JKI SM\0A\0D\0D\0AUsing the Right-click menu on the JKI SM Parts for increased productivity:\0D\0A- Select an item in the tree to make that frame visible\0D\0A- Click back and forward to navigate the history\0D\0A- Drag and drop frames to reorganize the order\0D\0A- Right-click on items in the tree-view to rename, duplicate, delete, etc.\0D\0A- Right-click on a state string and choose Goto State Frame to jump to that frame of the JKI SM.\0A- Right click on a state string or frame and choose Find Callers to find all callers of a state\0A- Right-click on a bundle or unbundle by name and choose Find Data Accessors to find all accessors of the data.\0D\0A\0D\0ASpecial thanks to Jim Carmody for open sourcing his CaseSelect tool as a launching off point for the JKI SM Editor."

Fix missing wiring to store the file refnum when opening a file in ZLIB Store File Continue.vi\0AVersion 5.0.2: Add a Low Level official API to store files in chunks into a ZIP file archive\0AVersion 5.0.1: Fix installation problems on various systems\0AVersion 5.0: Upgraded to latest zlib 1.3 sources and implemented a complete file manager layer to support long file paths as well as unicode file names.\0AVersion 4.3: Improved Unicode support for file names and strings in the ZIP directory.\0AVersion 4.2: Updated to zlib 1.2.11 and minizip 1.2 - June 14, 2019 and more 64-bit support\0AVersion 4.1: Updated to zlib 1.2.8 and added support for new cRIO targets\0AVersion 4.0: New palette menu structure\0AVersion 2.5.2: Adds support for the new palette locations of OpenG 4.x packages and removes dependency on ogrsc_dynamicpalette package.\0D\0AVersion 2.5.1: Fixes issue with broken VIs in LabVIEW 2009 due to calling (now) private config utilities.\0D\0AVersion 2.5: Changes license of LabVIEW sources from LGPL to BSD, Adds Memory Stream VIs to the palettes, Optimizes ZLIB Extract All Files to Dir, Fixes potential problem where error such as out of disk on finishing to add a file into an archive might get lost meaning that a corrupted archive could result without the user being informed about it, Fixes issue preventing adding files specified by UNC network path to zip archive.\0D\0AVersion 2.4 adds support for direct memory stream handling.\0D\0AVersion 2.3 adds support for transparent Mac Resource file handling through MacBinary encoding.\0D\0AVersion 2.2 adds support for appending files to an existing archive, deleting files from an archive and password support for adding and extracting files."
